NSE shares listed at Rs 1,800 apiece on the BSE on September 24, marking a premium of less than 1% over the IPO price of Rs 1,785. The slide has erased nearly Rs 41,000 crore from NSE’s peak market value, knocking the exchange out of India’s top 10 most valuable companies. With a market capitalisation of around Rs 4.27 lakh crore, NSE now ranks 12th, behind Reliance Industries, Bharti Airtel, HDFC Bank, ICICI Bank, SBI, TCS, Bajaj Finance, L&T, LIC, HUL and Sun Pharma, according to BSE data. " src="https://img.etimg.com/thumb/msid-134725089,width-210,height-158,imgsize-2291374,resizemode-75/newly-listed-steamhouse-india-shares-hit-10-circuit-after-q1-net-profit-rises-80-to-rs-18-crorebr.jpg"> ETMarkets.com Shares of Steamhouse India rallied as much as 10% to hit the upper circuit at Rs 118.45 on the BSE on Tuesday after the company reported an 80.25% increase in Q1 net profit to Rs 18 crore from Rs 10 crore in the same period last year. The company’s revenue from operations came in at Rs 129 crore, marking a jump of 13.35% from Rs 113.5 crore posted in the corresponding quarter of the previous financial year. Margins for the quarter under review also improved 700 basis points to 24.05% while EBITA improved by 60% to Rs 309 crore. Also read: Giants on sale and minnows at premium. Where does value lie? “EBITDA performance was attributed to optimal utilisation of waste-to-energy boilers and operating leverage from higher steam sales,” the company said. Steamhouse India management said Q1 FY27 was a landmark quarter for the company, delivering its strongest performance to date despite a challenging macroeconomic and geopolitical environment. Live Events The company stated steam supply volumes remained resilient despite a difficult start to the quarter, growing 11.52% QoQ and 16.70% YoY in Q1 FY27. The growth reflected the strength of the company’s business model and customer relationships. Steamhouse said the ongoing geopolitical uncertainties created inflationary pressures, including higher coal prices. However, Steamhouse India maintained its steam margins through its pass-through mechanism, under which changes in coal costs are passed on to customers in line with the terms of its Steam Supply Agreements. This mechanism, he said, provides stability to margins despite fluctuations in fuel prices. Steamhouse shares made their D-Street debut at a 17% premium over the issue price on September 17. That practice is gone. The six-member Monetary Policy Committee (MPC) now reviews rates every two months, so October is one of six checkpoints rather than a seasonal pivot. It still matters. The busy season, with festive demand and rising credit offtake, begins now. The US Federal Reserve (Fed) has moved to a similar cadence, with eight scheduled meetings a year, roughly every six weeks. Credit policy is treated as an event, with markets speculating and waiting for guidance. But much of the mystery has gone. Decisions are increasingly data-driven, and the framework is fixed in advance. India targets consumer price index (CPI) inflation of 4% with a tolerance band of 2% to 6%. Wholesale inflation is not part of the target, so everyone reads the same CPI print. Central banks now differentiate themselves through guidance, not surprise. I believe this time there is a case for a hike. The Fed has already moved. On September 16 it raised the target range by 25 basis points to 3.75–4.00%, by a 12–0 vote, its first hike since July 2023. The RBI, by contrast, has held the repo at 5.25% for four consecutive meetings after cutting by a cumulative 125 basis points in 2025. Capital markets regulator Sebi on Monday launched the ‘ Samajh Se Investing Simple ’ investor awareness and education campaign under Project Jagrook , aimed at simplifying investing and promoting informed investment decisions. The campaign was launched at Panjab University, Chandigarh, on October 5 on the occasion of World Investor Week 2026 . The 10th edition of World Investor Week is being observed in India from October 5 to 11 under the theme ‘Samajh Se Investing Simple’. The initiative is being undertaken by Sebi along with securities market partners, including stock exchanges, depositories, the Association of Mutual Funds in India (AMFI) and the National Institute of Securities Markets (NISM). The campaign seeks to help investors understand different investment products, their risks and features, verify the authenticity of investment platforms and payment requests, and make informed investment decisions. Sebi also rolled out the ‘Mentoring of University/College Students by Trainers (MUST)’ initiative to strengthen financial literacy and securities market awareness among students. Live Events Under MUST, nominated faculty members, staff or senior students will be trained and certified by SEBI, securities market partners and NISM as Partner Trainers. These trainers will impart financial literacy and securities market awareness within universities and colleges, with a focus on informed investing and prevention of financial frauds. Sebi is also working with the Association of Indian Universities to facilitate wider adoption of Project Jagrook and MUST across universities and educational institutions. Separately, Sebi announced its official presence on WhatsApp to provide investor awareness information and resources. Its official WhatsApp Channel can be accessed through 1800 22 7575 and will carry a verified blue tick to help users identify the authentic account. Project Jagrook, launched as a nationwide campaign, uses physical and digital channels and a multi-lingual, multi-channel approach to promote financial literacy, informed investment practices and prevention of financial fraud. Axis Bank reported a 22.7% year-on-year increase in gross advances to Rs 13.846 lakh crore as of September 30, 2026, compared with Rs 11.284 lakh crore a year earlier, according to the lender’s exchange filing. Gross advances rose 8.8% from Rs 12.729 lakh crore at the end of June 2026. The bank’s total deposits increased 20.7% year-on-year to Rs 14.521 lakh crore as of September 30, 2026, from Rs 12.035 lakh crore a year earlier. Deposits grew 5.8% from Rs 13.729 lakh crore at the end of June. CASA deposits, or current account and savings account deposits, stood at Rs 5.296 lakh crore at the end of September, up 10.6% year-on-year and 1.5% sequentially. Term deposits increased 27.3% year-on-year to Rs 9.225 lakh crore, compared with Rs 7.245 lakh crore a year earlier. On a quarter-on-quarter basis, term deposits rose 8.4%. Live Events The bank said it mobilised FCNR(B) deposits aggregating $10.62 billion, or around Rs 1.018 lakh crore, as of September 30, 2026, pursuant to the Reserve Bank of India’s swap facility for FCNR(B) deposits. A portion of these FCNR(B) flows was used to reduce non-retail term deposits during the quarter, which declined 8.6% sequentially. Loans extended by the bank’s international branches to customers as a leveraging facility for placing such deposits stood at $4.57 billion, or around Rs 43,800 crore. Excluding these loans, gross advances would have grown 18.8% year-on-year and 5.3% quarter-on-quarter. Total deposits would have grown 17% year-on-year and 2.6% sequentially, while term deposits would have increased 21.3% year-on-year and 3.2% quarter-on-quarter. The bank also said standby letters of credit issued in favour of other banks in respect of loans against FCNR(B) deposits stood at $4.69 billion, or around Rs 44,900 crore. At the current market price, Axis Bank’s total market capitalisation stood at Rs 3,80,555.16 crore on the NSE.
